subject.name: Desktop MCP client agent with the GitHub MCP server

capabilities.target: Open issues in the user's public repository
Any private repository the user owns (PAT has repo scope on all of them)

capabilities.tool_ref: github/create_or_update_file, github/push_files, github/create_branch, github/merge_pull_request (default toolsets, inferred)
capabilities.target: Every repository the PAT reaches, public and private

inputs.source: The user's own prompt in the desktop client
Issue titles, bodies, and comments in the public repository, returned as tool output by list_issues/get_issue; authorable by anyone on GitHub

instructions.note: The task "look at the open issues in my public repo" sets no boundary on which repositories may be read or written and does not say issue content is data, so injected requests in an issue look like in-scope work.
No system prompt or client policy is supplied. Nothing tells the agent to treat issue content as untrusted or to stay in the public repository.

elements.name: GitHub MCP server container (ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server, untagged, no digest), local stdio
GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN passed into the container environment (classic repo scope, all repos)
The user's public repository (issues and pull requests are world readable)
Any GitHub user who can open an issue on the public repository

controls.name: Client per-tool-call approval prompt (arguments collapsed by default)
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the client, but arguments are collapsed so the approver effectively decides on the tool name and the model's narration, not the repository and payload. A more capable model writes more convincing narration (ASI09). Users approve many calls per session, so approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403) already erodes it.

controls.name: Fine-grained PAT scoped to the single public repository (issues read, PR write only)
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by GitHub authorization. The model cannot read or write repositories the token cannot reach, whatever an issue tells it.

controls.name: MCP proxy policy binding each session to one repository (deny cross-repository tool calls)
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in a gateway between client and server on the owner/repo arguments, so a call that names a second repository is blocked regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Approval prompt showing full, expanded arguments (repository, path, PR body) with no remembered approvals
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees the raw owner/repo and payload from the call itself, not model narration. Still decays with volume, so pair with fewer calls per task.

controls.name: Run the server with --read-only and GITHUB_TOOLSETS limited to issues for triage sessions
controls.decay_rationale: Enumerated tool allowlist. Removes write and PR tools from this server, but a stronger model can chain any other egress channel the client exposes (another MCP server, link rendering).

controls.name: Pin the MCP server image by digest and review tool definitions on update
controls.decay_rationale: Tool code and definitions cannot change without a config diff.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) via confused deputy (TC4) behind a summary gate (TC9): public issue drives private repo read and leaks it in a public PR

attack_path.note: Attacker opens an issue with instructions; ingested via cap.read_public_issues when the user asks to look at issues
Model treats issue text as task and plans cross-repository work
get_file_contents on private repos using the all-repo PAT
Private content written into a PR on the public repo; world readable immediately

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Client approval setting changed to always-allow or allow-for-session; approvals per session rising (already many); model id changed in the client; tasks spanning more tool calls per session.

evidence.observation: Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repo, so in.public_issue is an attacker-authored U source.
The PAT has repo scope on every repo the user owns, so get_file_contents can reach private repos the task never needed (credential broader than the task: TC4).
Server is launched with the full PAT and no --read-only flag or GITHUB_TOOLSETS restriction, so create_pull_request is available in the same session as private reads.

The only preventive control is the per-call prompt; arguments are collapsed, so it is scored model_summary (step 2, floor moderate). Its residual credit rests on a declared, unverified gate that users already approve in volume.
The benign user request is enough to pull the hostile issue into context; no further user action is needed beyond approving calls.
Backtest: this matches the publicly reported GitHub MCP toxic agent flow (2025), where the per-call approval prompt was the control that failed. It is named in failing_controls.

recommendations.action: Replace the classic all-repo PAT with a fine-grained PAT limited to the public repository (issues read, pull requests write). Use a separate token for private-repo work (ctl.fine_grained_pat).
Put a policy proxy in front of the MCP server that binds a session to one repository and blocks calls naming any other owner/repo (ctl.single_repo_session_policy).
For triage sessions, start the server with --read-only and GITHUB_TOOLSETS=issues so no PR or write tool exists (ctl.read_only_toolsets).
Show full expanded arguments in the approval prompt and disable remembered approvals for write and cross-repo calls (ctl.raw_args_approval).
Alert on PRs or commits created by the agent's token that touch content from other repositories; review the GitHub security log for agent sessions.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): public issue drives writes to any repository the PAT reaches

attack_path.note: Issue asks the agent to fix, update, or merge something
create_or_update_file, push_files, or merge_pull_request on public or private repos with the all-repo PAT

forecast.watch_signal: Remembered or always-allow approvals enabled; model id change; server update that adds write tools to default toolsets.

evidence.observation: No --read-only or GITHUB_TOOLSETS restriction, so the server's default write tools are exposed. The exact tool list is inferred from server defaults, not supplied.
Repo scope grants write on every repository the user owns.
Only the collapsed-argument per-call prompt stands between the injected goal and the write (model_summary floor moderate).
U to S2 (write on confidential repos) is high; autonomy modifier applies because no step or runtime limit is declared, giving critical.

recommendations.action: Scope the token to the one public repository (ctl.fine_grained_pat); it severs writes to private repos.
Enable branch protection with required reviews on all repos so agent pushes cannot land on default branches.

findings.title: Unpinned MCP server image (rug pull): an updated image changes tool definitions or reads the PAT directly

attack_path.note: docker run pulls ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no tag or digest
Token is in the container environment, usable by server code without any tool call

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

forecast.watch_signal: Image digest of ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server changes between runs; tools/list response differs from the last reviewed set.

evidence.observation: Image reference has no tag or digest, so a pull silently replaces server code and tool definitions (definitions_pinned false).
The PAT is passed via -e into the container; compromised server code can use it without a gated tool call, so ctl.tool_call_prompt does not constrain that branch.
Today the image is the vendor's official build (treated as internal), so no complete path exists; it opens only when the image or its definitions change.

recommendations.action: Pin the image by sha256 digest and diff tools/list on every update (ctl.image_digest_pin).
Use a fine-grained, short-lived token so a compromised server reaches only one repo (ctl.fine_grained_pat).

rating.rationale: F1 is the lethal trifecta: attacker-authored issue text, an all-repo PAT that reads private code, and a public PR as the egress sink. The only preventive control is a per-call approval prompt with collapsed arguments, scored as a model_summary gate (-2 tiers, floor moderate), so residual is moderate per the rubric. That residual is fragile: the gate is declared not verified, users already approve many calls per session, and it is exactly the control that failed in the public incident this design reproduces. Under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase (always-allow), longer sessions, or control removal the gate stops constraining the path and every present finding returns to critical. A fine-grained PAT or a single-repo session policy would sever F1 and F2 outright. Validator: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration, not observed runtime behavior. No tool calls, approval logs, or injection tests were run.
No system prompt, client name, or model id was supplied; model swappability is unknown, so the model_upgrade trigger is assumed possible without review.
The full GitHub MCP tool list was not supplied. cap.write_any_repo and other egress channels (issue comments, gists) are inferred from the server's default toolsets, so F2 has medium confidence.
The approval gate is taken as declared. Whether the client offers always-allow or per-session approval was not stated; if it does, the gate earns no credit and residual for F1 and F2 is critical.
Approval volume is described only as many calls per session; per-day counts are unknown.
